reason: M8 is an auxiliary PMOS pull-up from VOUT1 to VDD controlled by the internal node net30; the output node VOUT1 already has a strong pull-up path via the cross-coupled PMOS M7 (gate=VOUT2, source=VDD).
impact_estimate: Removing M8 mainly reduces pull-up strength and regeneration speed on the VOUT1 side; the latch still functions correctly but may have slightly worse noise margin and slower decision time.

impact_estimate: Eliminating M5 symmetrically reduces pull-up strength and regeneration speed on the VOUT2 side; comparator functionality is preserved, though dynamic performance and offset symmetry may degrade modestly.

reason: M3 is a clock-gated NMOS that directly discharges the internal node net30 to VSS during reset, but net30 can still be discharged indirectly via the differential pair (M1/M2) and NMOS latch path during evaluation.
impact_estimate: Removing M3 will mainly slow or weaken the reset of net30 and can introduce some memory between clock cycles if the clock period is very short; for sufficiently slow clocks, the comparator still operates with only modest impact on accuracy.
